title: Domain and Metadata Semantics
current_summary: Current focus is the accepted domain/meta bridge-DSL reset: Functional Model requirements are the source for a smaller shared meta language between domain and IO, with adapter preservation and targeted deletion of historical sediment. The Domain Maintainer Contract is now canonical and its first pilot confirmed FK Relation Helpers and Lookup Enrichment as separate semantic owners (see CONC-DOMAIN-BOUNDARY-ROBUSTNESS / SIG-ACT-FK-LOOKUP-DMC-PILOT-SLICE-COMPLETE).
next_action: Create contract-backed FTR slices that derive bridge DSL portions from Functional Model use cases; do not golden-master current implementation workarounds. FTR-FK-REFERENCE-HELPER-SURFACE-CONSOLIDATION-P5 (choosing one canonical public helper-column surface between add_fk_helpers and add_lookup_helpers) remains queued, not started. It is no longer gated on the Domain Maintainer Contract's existence -- DMC is canonical and its first pilot (the FK/reference-helper family) is complete. That pilot's independent review (Cycle-0 finding F-004) distinguished this FTR's 'public surface consolidation' question from the separate 'semantic ownership merger' question the pilot answered; do not treat the pilot as having resolved or replaced this FTR. Do not broaden Trusted Ingress certification to the legacy add_fk_helpers formula producer as a substitute.
notes: This concern is a steering field, not a replacement for FTRs or concrete finding tracking. ADR-CONTRACT-FIRST-DOMAIN-META-REWRITE records the counter-conservative direction: low adoption makes breaking domain/meta changes acceptable when they reduce sediment and stabilize the bridge DSL.

title: Adapter and Spreadsheet Boundary
current_summary: Public/untrusted spreadsheet uploads are an intended deployment scenario, but serialized-input handling and parsed-carrier admission are separate boundaries: Trusted Ingress cannot prevent parser/library failure or resource exhaustion before carriers exist, and parser hardening cannot replace Trusted Ingress semantics. XLSX parser/resource-limit hardening remains open under FTR-XLSX-PARSER-RESOURCE-LIMITS-P4A; a documented boundary is not a hardened boundary.
next_action: Track the independently sequenced XLSX parser/resource-limit investigation under FTR-XLSX-PARSER-RESOURCE-LIMITS-P4A without treating it as E2, a Phase-E sub-slice, or a reason to block E2 merely by existing.
notes: Untrusted serialized bytes -> format/backend parser boundary -> parsed carriers -> Trusted Ingress -> conformant Domain payload. Public/untrusted XLSX upload readiness is not established: no XLSX parser limits are implemented. E1's hostile object-model probes are especially relevant to direct/programmatic/plugin carriers and do not prove that ordinary malicious XLSX bytes can instantiate attacker-selected Python classes or metaclasses. Runtime/operator trust, payload origin/trust, pipeline-description trust, and output-sink capability remain orthogonal accepted dimensions; payload trust is not newly introduced here.

title: User Surface and Adoption
current_summary: A maintained consumer proved configured Workbook View names and ordering across XLSX and ODS reimport, and the User Guide now documents the generic forward and inbound workflow; no missing capability surfaced. Grouped-XRef exact workbook projection is now also publicly reachable through a configured Workbook View and the router XLSX/ODS save paths (FTR-XREF-AXIS-MAPPINGS-P4A2 GX-5, accepted and Done).
next_action: Review after the next public-surface or release-preparation slice rather than turning every low-priority doc signal into a task.
notes: REVIEW-003 made this visible as a real concern thread, but it is not the current highest-pressure implementation slice.

title: Projection Ergonomics
current_summary: Dynamic column-axis crosstable projection now has an accepted baseline: axis mappings resolve live from source frames and are never persisted, flat and grouped axis-label projections compose around unchanged XRef over canonical string identity, and the grouped multi-row header roundtrips through XLSX and ODS via the backend-neutral core.ExactTable carrier. GX-5 public adoption is now accepted: grouped-XRef exact workbook projection is reachable through a configured Workbook View and the router XLSX/ODS save paths, so the FTR is Done. Remaining projection pressure is limited to later dynamic-view, discriminator-multiprojection, or editing gaps.
next_action: Keep further projection work tied to concrete dynamic-view, discriminator-multiprojection, or editing gaps; grouped-XRef adoption is complete and needs no follow-up FTR.
notes: Active as a strategic pressure field, but many concrete changes should wait for domain/meta clarification.

title: Backend Portability
current_summary: Current focus is XLSX/ODS parity, CSV/XML/JSON limitations, LibreOffice behavior, and backend capability clarity. The grouped exact multi-row header carrier reached required XLSX/ODS semantic parity through the shared TableBlock.header_grid and the backend-neutral, leaf-only core.ExactTable seam (GX-3b/GX-4), fresh evidence that the current parity strategy holds without a dedicated portability wave.
next_action: Keep as a watch concern until a consumer or release slice creates concrete backend pressure.
notes: Current evidence supports awareness rather than a dedicated portability wave.

title: Maintainability Hygiene
current_summary: Maintainability and local readability are judged through bounded reconstruction inside sound architecture, not mechanical cleanup. Module size, package surfaces, and module headers are inspection signals, not findings by themselves: split or add structure only on concrete responsibility, ownership, unstable-package-surface, reconstruction, or validation-locality evidence, and preserve cohesive long operations where extraction would increase non-local reasoning. The three-family Human Readability investigation validated this (XRef operation.py ~516 LOC and dense_axes.py ~411 LOC are cohesive and locally reconstructable).
next_action: Apply the bounded-reconstruction questions in ordinary reviews; open implementation only on concrete reader/ownership cost plus explicit authority. Add module headers where they give real orientation, not as a uniform mandate; do not run a mechanical cleanup wave. A Human Readability Guide or Sentinel experiment requires separate authorization.
notes: Many low/medium findings are heatmap signals for this concern rather than individual tasks. Reconciled 2026-08-04 with the three-family Human Readability evidence (REVSET-TOPIC-HUMAN-READABILITY, DEC-HUMAN-READABILITY-BOUNDED-RECONSTRUCTION): LOC alone is not a finding, and the module-size/modularization/header FTR records (FTR-REVIEW-001-MODULARIZATION-P4A, FTR-REVIEW-001-MODULE-HEADERS-P5, FTR-MAINTAINER-ENTRYPOINTS-AND-MODULE-BUDGETS-P5) were narrowed accordingly. Real package-surface, ownership, unrelated-responsibility, and agent read-window concerns remain valid.

title: Pipeline YAML Contract vs Callable Signature
current_summary: TODO -- clarify and enforce the boundary among callable signatures, generic binder-reserved fields, BoundStep metadata, and the public YAML step contract. registries/pipeline_step_registry.json mirrors callable parameters, but reserved YAML fields such as name may not reach the callable: the generic binders in pipeline/steps.py (make_builder_target_step, make_frames_target_step) reserve name for the BoundStep label and do not forward it inside **kwargs. Concretely, the Compact Multiaxis callable exposes name: str | None to set its own stable config_id, but YAML authors cannot currently reach that parameter through YAML name; expand/contract fall back to deriving config_id from output/relation.
next_action: Decide whether the registry needs separate callable and YAML parameter surfaces, explicit binder metadata, validation, or a namespaced callable config ID. The immediate Compact Multiaxis symptom (stale diagnostics trace IDs surviving a frame rename) is owned by FTR-COMPACT-MULTIAXIS-TRACE-LIFECYCLE-COMMANDS-P5; this concern tracks the broader registry/binder contract question, which is not scoped to any single FTR yet.
notes: Raised while implementing the Compact Multiaxis meta-persistence-correction and trace-lifecycle FTRs; verified directly against pipeline/build.py and pipeline/steps.py, not inferred from documentation alone. Evidence anchored by SIG-ACT-PIPELINE-YAML-CALLABLE-CONTRACT-TODO.

title: Domain Boundary Robustness
current_summary: Phase E (E1-E7) and Trusted Ingress documentation closure remain COMPLETE (unchanged from prior assessment). The Domain Maintainer Contract (DMC) has since completed its full design/review/correction/promotion lifecycle and is now canonical and active at docs/developer_guide/ch06_code_conventions/05_domain_maintainer_contract.adoc (SIG-ACT-DMC-CANONICAL-PROMOTED; DEC-DOMAIN-MAINTAINER-CONTRACT-CANONICAL). Hardening proceeds through bounded Domain areas selected one at a time; no whole-Domain family census exists or is required -- the semantic-ownership topology assessment remains evidence/navigation only (SIG-ACT-DOMAIN-TOPOLOGY-ASSESSMENT-EVIDENCE). The FK/reference-helper area was the first real DMC pilot: Cycle 0 and its first bounded hardening slice (the H5 FK-cleanup-to-Lookup-provenance-reconciliation handoff) are both independently reviewed and closed SLICE COMPLETE, exercising the first complete bounded DMC hardening loop end to end (SIG-ACT-FK-LOOKUP-DMC-PILOT-SLICE-COMPLETE). The derived-artifact research question the H5 slice raised is now resolved and closed: the FK Helper Deletion Authority nested subroutine ran research, an accepted design, Slices 1-5 runtime, an integration review, and Slice 6 documentation closure, all independently accepted with no claim ledger or new durable state introduced (SIG-ACT-FK-DELETION-AUTHORITY-CLOSED). TD-TRUSTED-INGRESS-INVARIANT-NAVIGATION-INDEX remains Open, Low severity, unaffected.
next_action: The FK helper deletion-authority subroutine is CLOSED; it is not a new architecture layer or continuing workstream (no claim ledger, claimant/reliance vocabulary, or global artifact identity was introduced). FK/reference-helper DMC hardening resumes at the exact point the H5 slice interrupted it: Family cycle 1 (remove remaining ontology), IN PROGRESS per docs/backlog/roadmap_domain_hardening_sequence.adoc. Candidates there include the deferred derived_column_policy.py Lookup-shape duplication (Cycle-0 finding F-002) and FTR-FK-REFERENCE-HELPER-SURFACE-CONSOLIDATION-P5's public-surface question (add_fk_helpers vs add_lookup_helpers), the latter now carrying recovered genealogy/capability evidence and a working (not yet decided) hypothesis that add_fk_helpers is the likely canonical surviving surface. Select the next bounded DMC hardening step at the maintainer's discretion; this closure does not itself authorize starting it.
notes: Steering field for the accepted Trusted Ingress contract and DEC-DOMAIN-BOUNDARY-ROBUSTNESS / DEC-TRUSTED-RUNTIME-AND-POLICY-AUTHORITY, and now also for the Domain Maintainer Contract era that follows Trusted Ingress closure. DEC-CLASSIFY-SAFELY-BEFORE-INSPECT has an E2-specific consequence: bounded issubclass(type(candidate), accepted_types) anchored on the real runtime type, scoped only to pandas.DataFrame and str -- not a generic issubclass safety claim. The independently tracked XLSX parser/resource-limit boundary remains unchanged. Current Domain physical-label authority is the open non-missing-like, hashable, unambiguously self-comparable predicate with uniqueness where scalar addressability requires it; no Scalar-only, string-only, or closed AxisAtom grammar is authorized generally, except the one deliberate role-scoped narrowing: a physical label nominated as a durable XRef row_keys/dense_axes selector reference must be exact native non-empty str. Row indexes remain positional traversal structure, not ordinary Scalar data. E1-E7 permanent current architecture owners: Semantic Model (06_project_semantic_model.adoc), Technical Model (ch06_architectural_layers/architectural_layers.adoc; ch08_architecture_details/internal_value_model.adoc), Developer Guide (ch06_code_conventions/04_trusted_ingress_extension.adoc), and docs/ai_info/interfaces_and_gates.adoc.
